verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and no level fails. demand-1 asks for confirmation that the v3 refactor leaves find_all_inheritors() results and lock order unchanged, since many commands use that function and no one has replied to v3. maintenance-fit-1 asks for a second caller and for a guard against choosing the cycle-raising function on a path that must tolerate cycles. Both are fixable, and a committer who knows the inheritance locking code can settle them.

brief.title: Add find_all_inheritors_ordered() for parent-before-child inheritance traversal
brief.problem: find_all_inheritors() can return a descendant before one of its ancestors when multiple inheritance gives both direct and indirect paths to a relation. Because of this, the fix in commit 0cd17fdd3c0 for altering CHECK constraint enforceability had to recurse upward through all ancestors. The audience is backend code, not end users.
brief.proposed_design: A new backend function, find_all_inheritors_ordered(), returns the inheritance tree in topological order using Kahn's algorithm, without recursion, and raises an error when it finds a cycle. In v3 it shares data gathering and locking with find_all_inheritors(). ALTER CONSTRAINT ... NOT ENFORCED uses it so each child checks only its direct parents; ENFORCED keeps find_all_inheritors().
user_visible_surface: C API: new function find_all_inheritors_ordered() declared in src/include/catalog/pg_inherits.h.
ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... NOT ENFORCED on an inheritance tree with a cycle now fails with an explicit cycle error instead of a stack depth error.
author_claims: The new function significantly simplifies the enforceability fix from commit 0cd17fdd3c0.
Other features that need parent-before-child traversal could use the function.
v3 keeps master's success and failure outcomes in Zsolt Parragi's isolation test, replacing only the stack depth error with a cycle error.
v3 shares data gathering and locking with find_all_inheritors(), so lock order stays the same.
brief.thread_state: solai v and Ewan Young reviewed v1 favorably; Zsolt Parragi showed concurrent ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT can create cycles, and Tom Lane asked for shared data gathering, both addressed in v3. No one has replied to v3, and blocking cycles at creation is left for a separate thread.
unclear: The material does not show whether Ewan Young's comment cleanup, typedefs.list entry and simplifications are in v3.
The text of the new cycle error message and its SQLSTATE are not given.
No reviewer has confirmed that the v3 refactor keeps find_all_inheritors() lock order and results unchanged.
The patch does not say whether v3 adds the isolation test from message #6.

objections.title: One caller does not yet justify a shared traversal refactor
objections.failure_scenario: v3 changes the internals of find_all_inheritors(), which TRUNCATE, ANALYZE, LOCK and other DDL use on every inheritance tree. If the shared data-gathering step changes lock or result order in some case, users of those commands see new deadlocks or different behaviour. They find out through a bug report long after commit, and the only gain is a cleaner ALTER CONSTRAINT ... NOT ENFORCED path.
objections.argument: The only user problem shown is code shape. The fix in 0cd17fdd3c0 already works, and v3 keeps master's success and failure outcomes (message #8), apart from the error text in a cycle case that is reachable only through concurrent ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT (messages #4, #10). The claim that other features need parent-before-child order (message #1) names no feature. Message #7 shows the two functions are tied by lock order, so the risk of the shared refactor reaches every caller of find_all_inheritors(), while the benefit stays with one code path.
objections.author_must_show: Which existing or planned callers besides the NOT ENFORCED path need parent-before-child order, and has anyone confirmed find_all_inheritors() results and lock order are unchanged?

critic.reasoning: v3 rewrites the internals of find_all_inheritors(), which many commands use, and no one has replied to v3 to confirm that results and lock order are unchanged. Tom Lane asked for the sharing, but that does not confirm it is correct.

objections.title: Second traversal API with different cycle semantics and one caller
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a DDL path and calls find_all_inheritors_ordered() because it wants parent-before-child order. Tests pass, since cycles appear only through concurrent ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT. Months later a user with such a cycle finds that the command now errors where find_all_inheritors() would have coped.
objections.argument: After v3, pg_inherits.h exports two functions that return the same set of OIDs but differ on cycles: one tolerates them, the other raises an error (message #5, message #8). The only rule for choosing between them is a header comment. The patch has one caller, and even ALTER CONSTRAINT splits by direction because the ordered function is unsafe for ENFORCED (message #6, message #8). The claim that other features could use it names no second caller.
objections.author_must_show: Which other current or planned callers need ordered traversal, and how would a reviewer catch a caller that picks the cycle-raising function on a path where cycles must be tolerated?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 shows this hazard already occurred: v2 used the ordered function for ENFORCED and changed an outcome that master allowed. The thread names no second caller, and only a header comment guides the choice between the two functions.

refuted.title: Cycle semantics fixed before the cycle-prevention work is decided
refuted.failure_scenario: The patch is committed with a cycle error in the new API and a split ENFORCED/NOT ENFORCED code path. The separate thread then blocks cycles at creation time. The error branch becomes dead code, the direction split serves no purpose, and both stay in tablecmds.c because extensions may already call the exported function.
refuted.argument: Tom Lane said in message #7 he would rather block cycles than make parts of the system cope, and the author agreed to look into it in message #9. The v3 design is shaped by the cycle case: an error instead of an Assert, plus two traversals in one command. If prevention lands, the simpler design from v1 would be the right one. No one has replied to v3.
refuted.author_must_show: If concurrent INHERIT cycles are blocked later, would this API and the ENFORCED/NOT ENFORCED split stay as they are, or should prevention be settled first?

critic.reasoning: Blocking cycles at creation does not remove cycles already present in existing clusters, so the error branch stays reachable and v1's Assert would still be wrong. The ENFORCED/NOT ENFORCED split is internal to tablecmds.c and can be removed later whatever extensions call.

refuted.title: Committed upward recursion already gives correct results; new API has one caller
refuted.failure_scenario: After commit, pg_inherits.c exports two traversal functions whose lock order is coupled through a shared helper, and the ordered one has one caller. A later change to the helper for one caller can change results or lock order for the other, and this shows up only as a deadlock report or a wrong conenforced value.
refuted.argument: Commit 0cd17fdd3c0 already fixes the enforceability bug with upward recursion over find_all_inheritors(), so the user-visible need is met. The patch is a cleanup of that one call site, and message #1 offers other users only as "could potentially benefit". Message #7 shows why the coupling matters: the two traversals must lock in the same order. v3 shares the data gathering, but no reviewer has confirmed it, and the patch still adds a permanent exported API for one caller.
refuted.author_must_show: Which other current callers would switch to parent-before-child order, or why is a sort inside tablecmds.c over find_all_inheritors() output not enough?

critic.reasoning: The scenario treats the shared helper as the risk, but Tom Lane asked for that sharing in message #7 so the two traversals cannot diverge in lock order. The one-caller point is a duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, and the unconfirmed refactor is covered by demand-1.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch exports a new function, find_all_inheritors_ordered(), in src/include/catalog/pg_inherits.h.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Two traversal functions with different cycle behaviour share data gathering and locking, and the ordered one has one caller.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Has anyone confirmed that find_all_inheritors() returns the same results and takes locks in the same order after the v3 refactor, and how was that checked?
Which existing or planned callers besides the NOT ENFORCED path need parent-before-child order?
How would a reviewer catch a new caller that uses find_all_inheritors_ordered() on a path where an inheritance cycle must be tolerated?
What are the message text and SQLSTATE of the new cycle error?
Does v3 include the isolation test from message #6 and the comment cleanup and typedefs.list entry from message #3?

committability.owner_note: Tom Lane asked for shared data gathering in message #7 but has not replied to v3. The owner needs to know inheritance traversal and DDL lock order.
committability.liability: The owner signs for unchanged lock order and results in find_all_inheritors(), which TRUNCATE, ANALYZE, LOCK and other DDL use, and for a new exported function that extensions may call.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 and v3 in response to review and agreed in message #9 to look into blocking cycles at creation in a separate thread.

priority.reason: The patch is a backend cleanup of one call site, about 19 KiB across pg_inherits.c and tablecmds.c, with no end-user surface beyond one error message. Review cost is medium because the v3 refactor changes the internals of find_all_inheritors() and lock order needs a careful read.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check whether v3 keeps find_all_inheritors() lock order and results, or whether the cycle check covers every cycle shape. Only 3 of 10 messages were shown in full.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix ALTER TABLE DROP EXPRESSION with ONLY option
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP EXPRESSION work on inheritance trees with more than one level, where it now fails with "must be applied to child tables too". It adds a `!recursing` check in ATPrepDropExpression() so the ONLY check runs only for the table named in the command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Peter Eisentraut asked why tablecmds.c passes recurse = false when recursing, and suggested a more consistent use of the two flags would make the existing code work. Tom Lane said that if the flags matter here, DROP EXPRESSION should not use ATSimpleRecursion. The author replied in December 2025 that v3 is correct, and no later reply appears before the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent ALTER TABLE DROP NOT NULL on child tables if parent column has it
precedents_retrieved.summary: Prevent ALTER TABLE ... DROP NOT NULL on a child table when the same column in a parent table is marked NOT NULL, so that the constraint can only be dropped from the parent. The patch added a function in pg_inherits.c to list a relation's parents and a new index on pg_inherits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the approach was wrong because it does not help decide whether to propagate DROP NOT NULL from a parent to its children, and pointed to the earlier plan of storing NOT NULL constraints in pg_constraint with inheritance counts as CHECK constraints do. After Vitaly Burovoy reported that he was writing such a patch, which already forbids dropping inherited NOT NULLs, the author withdrew his proposal in favour of that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't sound like the right approach; in particular, it won't really
help for deciding whether to propagate a DROP NOT NULL on a parent rel to
its children.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
Reverted commit(s): Allow page lock to conflict among parallel group members.; Add assert to ensure that page locks don't participate in deadlock cycle.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the work done by commits 3ba59ccc89 and 72e78d831a.
Those commits were incorrect in asserting that we never acquire any other
heavy-weight lock after acquring page lock other than relation extension
lock. We can acquire a lock on catalogs while doing catalog look up after
acquring page lock.

This won't impact any existing feature but we need to think some other way
to achieve this before parallelizing other write operations or even
improving the parallelism in vacuum (like allowing multiple workers
for an index).

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix alter subscription concurrency errors
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Amit Kapila, Alvaro Herrera, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixed "tuple concurrently updated" errors from concurrent ALTER/DROP SUBSCRIPTION statements on the same subscription by re-fetching the subscription tuple after acquiring its lock, using a retry loop modeled on dbcommands.c. A later version also allowed ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... OWNER TO to run concurrently with the other subscription commands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected that adding lock-and-retry lookup code specific to subscriptions does not scale, since the same problem affects other object types. Alvaro Herrera suggested using get_object_address() instead, and Tom Lane added that this might first require improving its error reporting. The author did not post an updated version for several commitfests. He then said his own test-flakiness problem had been worked around and that he was not motivated to address the issue for all DDL commands, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think the patch as-submitted is pretty uninteresting, mainly because the
design of adding bespoke lock code for subscription objects doesn't scale.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow meson to find ICU in non-standard location
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes meson so that it finds ICU in a non-standard location when -Dextra_lib_dirs and -Dextra_include_dirs are given, by searching for the library directly. The author was unsure about the approach, partly because meson then reports only "YES" and not the ICU version found.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it because setting -Dextra_lib_dirs, as Jacob Champion suggested, already worked with ICU 72 without the patch. Andres Freund had also pointed to -Dpkg_config_path, which finds ICU but did not add the RPATH in the author's test. The author said a clearer solution or doc updates would still help others.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Obviously we'd like a little better solution so that others don't get
confused, but it's not really a problem for me any more.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow subfield references without parentheses
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets column references with three or more identifiers be read as a correlation name, a column and one or more composite-type fields, as the SQL standard allows, so `A.B.C` can mean `(A.B).C`. The correlation must be an explicit alias, and the parser raises an error when both readings apply.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane raised possible new ambiguity but agreed with raising an error, and Ashutosh Bapat suggested building the reference through transformIndirection(). The patch also still had TODOs for documentation and for SQL and PL/pgSQL parameters, and no reply after 2024-12-13 is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: CHECK constraint deferrable Support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets CHECK constraints be declared DEFERRABLE and INITIALLY DEFERRED, as the SQL standard allows, so SET CONSTRAINTS can delay a CHECK until commit. Rows that fail a deferrable CHECK are rechecked at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CHECK implementation assumes constraints are immutable, and the patch does not change that assumption, so he called the feature a toy. Others then argued it should be dropped or combined with deferrable NOT NULL, which Robert Haas and Vik Fearing disputed. Dean Rasheed also reported open bugs, including a deferred constraint that still failed immediately and a wrong constraint-exclusion result. The visible messages do not show why the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I continue to assert that basing this feature on the current CHECK implementation will produce nothing but a toy feature, that's not only of little practical use but will be an active foot-gun for people who expect it to do more than it can.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
Reverted commit(s): Reject concurrent sequence refreshes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P8] concerns blocking DROP NOT NULL on child tables, and its recorded reason does not apply to an ordered traversal function. The thread mentions only the earlier bug fix from message #1 (commit 0cd17fdd3c0), which this patch builds on. Tom Lane's shared data-gathering request in message #7 is reported as addressed in v3.

From the standards and compatibility angle the proposal has almost no user-facing surface: no syntax, keyword, GUC, catalog, pg_dump or psql change. The one visible change is a cycle error in place of a stack depth error, and only in an inheritance cycle that a race between concurrent ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT commands can create (message #4). Tom Lane wants such cycles blocked instead of supported (message #7). v3 keeps master's success and failure outcomes in the message #6 test (message #8), but that test covers two permutations and does not show that outcomes match for every cycle shape. The SQLSTATE and wording of the new error are not shown, which is a detail-level point.

The proposal adds no persistent or cross-node state. It does not change the on-disk format, WAL records, catalogs, catversion or the wire protocol, and existing ABI is unaffected because it only adds one new backend function to pg_inherits.h. Lock order across backends is the one cross-process concern; message #7 raised it and v3 answers it with shared data gathering, which only a code read can confirm.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It adds an internal C traversal function and changes how ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... NOT ENFORCED walks an inheritance tree that the caller must already own. Per message #9, v3 shares locking with find_all_inheritors(), so it takes no new locks and opens no new resource path. The only user-visible change replaces a stack depth error with a cycle error in a case that already fails on master (message #8). Building a cycle needs ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT on the tables involved, so an unprivileged user gains no new way to block another owner's DDL. One point could not be checked without the code: whether the cycle error names only relations the caller can already see.
There is no hot-path cost, since this is DDL-only. Tom Lane's lock-order concern is addressed in v3 according to message #9, but no reviewer has confirmed it.
Postgres has no existing parent-before-child traversal, and no extension can provide one, so the only point from this angle is that the committed fix already meets the need.
This is backend cleanup with no end-user demand expected. The one objection asks for a second caller or proof that existing callers are unaffected. It does not claim the idea is unwanted.
